Sets the most frames per second that [Flip](Flip) lets the program show. This is a BlitzLLVM extension. It replaces the fragile loop of [CreateTimer](CreateTimer) and [WaitTimer](WaitTimer): the wait is kept by deadlines that follow the last frame, so one slow frame does not push every later frame back and a 60 Hz limit stays at 60 frames per second.

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 640, 480, 32, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
SetGraphicsRefreshRate 120 ; no more than 120 frames per second
While Not KeyHit(1)
	RenderWorld
	Flip 1 ; waits for the display and keeps the limit
Wend
```

[Flip](Flip) 0 is never limited. [Flip](Flip) 1 waits for the display and keeps the limit. [Flip](Flip) 2 never makes the program wait: the program renders as fast as it can, and a frame that is flipped sooner than the limit allows is drawn but not shown, so the display gets the newest frame at most as often as the limit.
@param rate  The most frames per second, up to 100000. 0 is no limit, which is also the start value. Anything else is a runtime error.
